tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

Upload the ONBOARDING.md in the current directory and return a share link teammates can open in Claude Code. Call this after the user has confirmed the final content.

When called with the default mode='check': if a local ONBOARDING.md is present, uploads it to the most-recently-updated org guide (or creates one if none exist) and returns a fresh link. If no local file is present, returns the existing link without uploading (status: has_existing).

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab to test responsive layouts. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_agile_boards
entries.description:
Get jira agile boards by name, project key, or type.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    board_name: Name of the board (fuzzy search).
    project_key: Project key.
    board_type: Board type ('scrum' or 'kanban').
    start_at: Starting index.
    limit: Maximum results.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of board objects.

board_name.description: (Optional) The name of board, support fuzzy search

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue
entries.description:
Get details of a specific Jira issue including its Epic links and relationship information.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: Jira issue key.
    fields: Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'), a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'), '*all' for all fields, or omitted for essentials.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    comment_limit: Maximum number of comments.
    properties: Issue properties to return.
    update_history: Whether to update issue view history.

Returns:
    JSON string representing the Jira issue object.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the Jira client is not configured or available.

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'). You may also provide a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'). Use '*all' for all fields (including custom fields), or omit for essential fields only.

expand.description: (Optional) Fields to expand. Examples: 'renderedFields' (for rendered content), 'transitions' (for available status transitions), 'changelog' (for history)

comment_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to include (0 or null for no comments)

properties.description: (Optional) A comma-separated list of issue properties to return

update_history.description: Whether to update the issue view history for the requesting user

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_sprint_issues
entries.description:
Get jira issues from sprint.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    sprint_id: The ID of the sprint.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return.
    start_at: Starting index.
    limit: Maximum results.

Returns:
    JSON string representing the search results including pagination info.

fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return in the results. Use '*all' for all fields, or specify individual fields like 'summary,status,assignee,priority'

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_sprints_from_board
entries.description:
Get jira sprints from board by state.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    board_id: The ID of the board.
    state: Sprint state ('active', 'future', 'closed'). If None, returns all sprints.
    start_at: Starting index.
    limit: Maximum results.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of sprint objects.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_search
entries.description:
Search Jira issues using JQL (Jira Query Language).

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    jql: JQL query string.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return.
    limit: Maximum number of results.
    start_at: Starting index for pagination.
    projects_filter: Comma-separated list of project keys to filter by.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    page_token: Pagination token from a previous search result (Cloud only).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the search results including pagination info.

jql.description:
JQL query string (Jira Query Language). Examples:
- Find Epics: "issuetype = Epic AND project = PROJ"
- Find issues in Epic: "parent = PROJ-123"
- Find by status: "status = 'In Progress' AND project = PROJ"
- Find by assignee: "assignee = currentUser()"
- Find recently updated: "updated >= -7d AND project = PROJ"
- Find by label: "labels = frontend AND project = PROJ"
- Find by priority: "priority = High AND project = PROJ"

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated fields to return in the results. Use '*all' for all fields, or specify individual fields like 'summary,status,assignee,priority'

projects_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of project keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER if provided.

page_token.description: (Optional) Pagination token from a previous search result. Cloud only — Server/DC uses start_at for pagination.

input.prompt:
You are auditing the Zimmermann PWA Kit codebase at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (current branch feature/SFCC-11_cart — note this branch has a lot of uncommitted/unmerged cart work; check BOTH the current working tree AND the `develop` branch state, and say which is which).

GOAL: Determine, for five upcoming Sprint 6 stories, what already exists in the codebase that can be reused, and what has to be built from scratch. This directly drives build sequencing, so precision matters.

THE FIVE STORIES:
1. SFCC-743 "Product Card Group – PWA Component" — a component rendering an optional section header (title + link) and a responsive row of ProductCard components. Props: display (3|4|6), size (Desktop|Mobile), showTitleAndLink, showLink, title, linkLabel. Tablet: display=4 renders only 3 cards.
2. SFCC-874 "Product Card Group with Lookbook – PWA Component" — section header + a large lookbook image slot on the left + N product card slots. Props: size, grid (3|4), qty (2|3|5), showTitleAndLink, cardType (Product|Editorial). qty=5 → 2x2 grid of tiles. Tablet: lookbook full-width top, tiles below; qty=5 renders only 3 small cards on tablet. Mentions `imageGroup.showCarousel` and `imageGroup.showSlideIndicator` props on desktop.
3. SFCC-749 "Breadcrumb and SEO – PWA Kit Component" — breadcrumb on every page generated from page context; plus a collapsible SEO text block (title, intro, READ MORE/READ LESS expanding a body) rendered above the footer on category pages, content from Contentful keyed by category ID.
4. SFCC-748 "Breadcrumb and SEO – Contentful Component" — the Contentful content type/schema for the above: category ID (mandatory), title, intro text, expanded SEO body, locale support.
5. SFCC-801 "global/country-currency-selector — PWA Component" — right-anchored slide-in drawer, full-width on mobile, dark overlay, sticky header + sticky Confirm/Apply footer, scrolling country list grouped by collapsible region accordions (region label + chevron; rows with flag icon, country name, right-aligned currency code, radio select), optional description, optional language selector radio section, onConfirm(country, locale) callback, focus trap, aria-expanded.

WHAT TO REPORT PER STORY:
- Which existing components/atoms/molecules/organisms under overrides/app/components/ (especially ui-kits/) can be reused, with exact paths. Look hard for: product card / product tile, breadcrumb, accordion, drawer, checkbox/radio, link, button, image gallery/carousel, icons (flag icons?), table, chip, section headers.
- Which existing theme recipes exist (overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts registrations, and co-located *.css.ts files).
- Which base Salesforce retail-react-app files would need the "copy-first" override treatment (check node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/ for breadcrumb, etc.), since the project rule requires copying base files to overrides/ as a separate gated step BEFORE functional changes. This is a real schedule cost — flag every story that needs it.
- Existing Contentful integration: what content types are already defined in scripts/contentful/content-types/, how components are registered with Contentful (look at overrides/app/components/contentful/), and what SFCC-748 would add.
- Any existing breadcrumb usage in the app today, and whether routes/page context data needed to generate a breadcrumb programmatically is already available.
- Whether a country/region/locale list already exists (overrides/app/config/countries.ts, config/sites.js) and what shape it has.
- Whether flag icons exist in overrides/app/components/icons.

ALSO REPORT: a blunt assessment of which of the five shares the most implementation surface with which others — i.e. if built back-to-back, what concretely gets reused. Be specific (named files/components), not hand-wavy.

Read-only. Do NOT modify any files. Do not commit anything.

echo "PR   author          commits  first-commit  merged      span" && for pr in 116 112 120 117 113 111 109 108 103; do
  dates=$(gh api "repos/:owner/:repo/pulls/$pr/commits" --paginate -q '.[].commit.committer.date' 2>/dev/null | sort)

  auth=$(echo "$meta" | cut -f1); merged=$(echo "$meta" | cut -f2 | cut -c1-10)
  if [ -n "$first" ] && [ -n "$merged" ]; then
    span=$(( ( $(date -j -f "%Y-%m-%d" "$merged" "+%s") - $(date -j -f "%Y-%m-%d" "$first" "+%s") ) / 86400 ))
    printf "#%-4s %-15s %-8s %-13s %-11s %sd\n" "$pr" "${auth:0:14}" "$n" "$first" "$merged" "$span"
  fi
done

**Props — `ZimmProductCardProps = ZimmProductCardBaseProps & (union of 4 variations)`**

Base (all required unless marked `?`):
| prop | type |
|---|---|
| `id` | `string` |
| `href` | `string` (caller pre-site-prefixes) |
| `name` | `string` |
| `headingLevel` | `'h1' \| 'h2' \| 'h3'` |

Variations (discriminant `variation`):
- `'plp'` — `onAddToBag?`, `sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[]`, `selectedSizeChipValue?: string`, `onSizeChipSelect?: (v: string) => void`
- `'home'` — no extra fields
- `'wishlist'` — `colour: string` (**required**), `size: string` (**required**), `onRemove: () => void` (**required**), `onAddToBag?`, + the same size-chip trio
- `'recentlyViewed'` — no extra fields

**Editorial variant: DOES NOT EXIST.** There are exactly four variations, all product-shaped. Every layout decision is table-driven via `VARIATION_CONFIG` (index.tsx:413-473) with 12 boolean flags (`showBag`, `showAttributes`, `showSizeChips`, `hoverHidesPrice`, `hoverRevealsPrice`, `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`, `showRemove`, `hideBagOnMobile`, `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable`, `showBadge`, `showHoverImageSwap`, `showContent`). The render body contains zero `if`/`switch` on `variation` — **adding an SFCC-874 `cardType: 'Editorial'` is a one-row addition to `VARIATION_CONFIG` + one union member, touching no JSX.** The file's own docblock (lines 177-184) pre-authorises exactly this: *"editorial and landing pages… when it is scoped, it needs its own `VARIATION_CONFIG` row (both flags `false`)"*.

**Data shape consumed:** a flat, pre-formatted view-model — prices already currency-formatted strings, `href` already site-prefixed, images already `{src, alt}`. No SFCC/Contentful types reach this component.

## 2b. `zimmProductCardMedia` — molecule — **this is where the carousel already lives**

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx`
Recipe: `.../zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` — yes. `parts: ['root','scrollContainer','slide','image','hoverSwapBase','hoverSwapOverlay','badge','badgeLabel','close','carousel','arrowButton','indicatorWrapper']`. Slide aspect ratio hardcoded `2 / 3`.

**Exports:** `ZimmProductCardMedia` (named + default), `ZimmProductCardMediaImage`, `ZimmProductCardMediaProps`.

Props: `primaryImage` (req), `primaryImageFallbacks?`, `hoverImage?`, `images?`, `swapOnHover` (**required** bool), `showControls` (**required** bool), `badge?`, `onRemove?`, `removeLabel?`, `priority?`, `widths?`, `quality?: number|null`, `onClick?`.

**YES — carousel, multi-image AND hover-swap, all three, already built and shipped:**
- **Carousel**: native CSS scroll-snap (`overflowX: auto`, `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'`, `scrollSnapAlign: 'start'`, `WebkitOverflowScrolling: 'touch'`, scrollbar hidden). Activates purely off `images.length > 1`.
- **Prev/next arrows**: gated by `showControls && totalSlides > 1`; `goToRelativeSlide()` wraps modulo and calls `container.scrollTo({left: index * clientWidth, behavior:'smooth'})`.

- **Index clamping** on slide-count shrink; **cascading `onError` fallback** through `primaryImageFallbacks` or the gallery sequence.

This is a **complete, self-contained, reusable intra-card carousel**. `imageGroup.showCarousel` / `imageGroup.showSlideIndicator` (SFCC-874) map almost one-to-one onto `showControls` and "render indicator when `totalSlides > 1`" — the only genuine gap is that the indicator is **unconditional** today (`totalSlides > 1`, no prop), so `showSlideIndicator` needs a new optional prop, and neither flag is currently exposed through the `ZimmProductCard` organism (it hardcodes `showControls` and never forwards an indicator flag).

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx`

Each `card` = `flex:'0 0 auto'` with `width` as a **percentage share** — `50%` base / `33.3333%` ≥768px / `20%` ≥1024px, derived from `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS = {base:2, md:3, xl:5}` (`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/constants/index.ts:56`), plus `minWidth: 12.5rem`.

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/index.tsx`

The 4-up desktop grid geometry for SFCC-743's `display=4` is already in this repo.

### Blunt gap statement vs SFCC-743

| SFCC-743 requirement | Status |
|---|---|
| Responsive row of `ProductCard`s | **Exists twice, neither reusable as-is.** Rail = flex percentage-share (variation-locked to `recentlyViewed`); Grid = CSS Grid (2/3/4). PLP = a third approach, Chakra `SimpleGrid columns={[2,2,4,5]}` at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:1360`. **Three divergent implementations of "row of cards" already.** |
| Section header (title + link) | **Exists, but only inside the Rail** as `title`/`seeAllHref`/`seeAllLabel`. Not extracted, not shared. The Grid deliberately does **not** share it (documented decision, different Figma node). |
| `showTitleAndLink` / `showLink` | **Does not exist.** Zero repo hits. The Rail's equivalent is implicit (`seeAllHref && seeAllLabel` truthiness), not an explicit boolean. |

| `size` = Desktop\|Mobile | **Does not exist.** Every existing component derives breakpoint from CSS media queries or `useMediaQuery`, never from a prop. |

## 4. `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`

Two exported hooks plus three exported pure helpers. Raw `fetch` against the REST CDA — no SDK.

```ts
useContentfulEntry<T>(entryId: string, preview = false, locale?: string)
  → { data: T | null, isLoading: boolean, error: Error | null }

useContentfulEntries<T>(
  contentType: string,
  preview = false,
  locale?: string,
  filter?: string,     // raw Contentful search-param string
  enabled = true,
  include = 2,
) → { data: T[] | null, isLoading: boolean, error: Error | null }
```

Answers to your specific questions:
- **`content_type` filtering: yes.** `useContentfulEntries` builds `content_type=${contentType}` and appends `&${filter}` when provided (line 219).
- **Arbitrary field filtering: yes, and already in production use.** The `filter` param is passed through verbatim as Contentful Search Parameters. `fields.categoryId=X` would work today with **zero hook changes**. Precedents: `'fields.placement=benefits'` in `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmBenefits/index.tsx:29`, and `fields.key[in]=…&select=sys,fields` in `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.ts:54-57`.
  - Caller must `encodeURIComponent` the value itself — `buildContentfulUrl` does **not** encode the filter string.
- **Locale: per-request, optional.** `buildContentfulUrl(query, config, preview, locale, include)` appends `&locale=${encodeURIComponent(locale)}` only when `locale` is truthy; omitted ⇒ Contentful's default locale. `locale` is in the effect dep array, so a locale change re-fetches and resets `data`/`error` to null first.
- **Return shape:** `{ data, isLoading, error }`. `data` is the raw Contentful item(s) run through `resolveLinkedAssets`, which recursively inlines `includes.Asset` / `includes.Entry` into `fields`, guards cycles via a `visitedIds` set, and **deletes unresolved/cyclic Entry links** (arrays filter them out) rather than leaving Link stubs.
- Preview: `preview=true` swaps host to `preview.contentful.com` and uses `previewAccessToken`.
- `getValidatedContentfulConfig()` **throws** `'Contentful configuration missing'` if `spaceId`/`accessToken` absent — caught into `error` state.

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.test.ts` — vitest; covers locale-change state handling, `getValidatedContentfulConfig`, `buildContentfulUrl`, `resolveLinkedAssets`.

This is one of 8 conflicted files on branch `feature/SFCC-11_cart` (also: `zimmButton/index.tsx`, `pages/product-list/index.tsx`, `theme/components/index.ts`, and 4 registry files).

The `develop` version (`git show develop:...`, 265 lines, clean) has the same `parts` array, the same `overlay`, and a simpler `prompt` variant — **no footer part in either.** The conflict does not affect SFCC-801's decisions either way.

**Verdict: reusable as-is for shell + overlay + focus trap + mobile full-width + sticky header. Needs a new `footer` part (or an organism that owns its own sticky footer) for Confirm/Apply.**

### 9. `ZimmAccordion` — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmAccordion/index.tsx`

```ts
export type ZimmAccordionItem = { id: string; label: string; content: React.ReactNode; alwaysVisibleContent?: React.ReactNode };
type ZimmAccordionProps = { items: readonly ZimmAccordionItem[]; defaultExpandedId?: string };
```
- Built on Chakra `Accordion`/`AccordionItem`/`AccordionButton`/`AccordionPanel`. **Yes.**
- **Chevron: yes** — swaps `ChevronUpIcon`/`ChevronDownIcon` (not a CSS rotation; the two Zimmermann glyphs are distinct shapes).
- **`aria-expanded`: yes, free** — Chakra's `AccordionButton` is a real `<button>` and sets it. The header also has a `_focusVisible` outline in `zimmAccordion.css.ts`.
- **Single-open only.** `<Accordion allowToggle defaultIndex={...}>` — no `allowMultiple`, and `ZimmAccordionProps` exposes no way to opt in. Uncontrolled (no `onChange` out).
- `alwaysVisibleContent` renders a collapsed-state summary outside the panel — useful if you want "2 selected" style summaries per region.

**Blunt assessment: usable, but not quite as-is.** It will render region label + chevron + `aria-expanded` correctly with zero work. Two caveats: (a) **single-open** means expanding "Europe" collapses "Americas" — if the design shows multiple regions open, that is a **new `allowMultiple` prop** on the atom (small, additive change); (b) it's **uncontrolled**, so the parent cannot auto-expand the region containing the shopper's current country after mount, nor react to a search filter. If SFCC-801 needs either, you need a controlled variant. Call it **"reusable with a new variant."**

### 10. RADIO — build from scratch. Definitively.

- **No radio atom exists.** `ls overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/` → 28 atoms, none radio. `find overrides -iname "*radio*"` → zero results.
- **Chakra `Radio`/`RadioGroup` in `overrides/`:** only two call sites, both base-file overrides, neither a Zimmermann component — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:1548` (delivery vs. pickup, raw unstyled Chakra) and an unused import in `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:40`. There is **no Zimmermann-styled Radio recipe** in `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (63 recipes registered, no Radio).
- `ZimmCheckbox` (`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmCheckbox/index.tsx`), props: `{ value, label, isChecked, onChange(value, isCurrentlySelected), hitCount?, swatchColour? }`. It is **not** a good base to adapt: it's built on Chakra `Checkbox`, it hardcodes filter-specific semantics (`hitCount === 0 && !isChecked → return null`, and an `aria-label` of "Add filter"/"Remove filter" from `app/utils/refinementValues`), and it inlines ~90 lines of `sx` rather than using a recipe — so it isn't even conformant with the house pattern. Its square-indicator styling is worth *reading* for visual language, not extending.
- **The right precedent instead:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeChip/index.tsx` and `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx` — both are `chakra.button` with `role="radio"` + `aria-checked` + `tabIndex` driven by a parent group (`zimmSizeChipGroup`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup`) that owns roving-tabindex keyboard orchestration. That atom/group split is the established house pattern for single-select.

**Verdict: build from scratch.** Either a `ZimmRadio` atom + recipe, or (more likely, given the row is flag + name + currency + indicator) a `ZimmCountryRow` with `role="radio"`, wrapped in a `role="radiogroup"` parent that handles arrow keys — following `zimmSizeChipGroup`.

### 11. Drawer content organisms

**`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.tsx`** (SFCC-847) — the closest structural match, and the file to model SFCC-801 on.
```ts
type ZimmFiltersDrawerContentProps = {
  facetGroups: readonly FilterFacetGroup[];  // = ZimmAccordionItem[]
  initialExpandedId?: string;
  onClear: () => void;
  onApply: () => void;
  clearLabel?: string;   // default 'CLEAR'
  applyLabel?: string;   // default 'APPLY'
};
```
What it already gives you: collapsible groups via `ZimmAccordion`, a two-button action row (`secondary` CLEAR + `primary` APPLY, `size="large"` = 52px, `fullWidth`), a caller-owns-state contract, and a recipe with responsive padding (16px mobile / 64px md+) and a 64px body↔footer gap.

**What it does NOT give you — read this carefully, it contradicts the assumption in your brief:**

**The footer is NOT sticky.** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmFiltersDrawerContent/zimmFiltersDrawerContent.css.ts` lines 9-14 state the intent explicitly: *"content-container is `shrink-0` in Figma — it flows naturally with its content rather than filling the drawer to the bottom. Buttons appear immediately after the accordion group (64px gap)... The parent ZimmDrawer wrapper owns `overflow-y: auto` so the entire content area (accordions + buttons) scrolls together."* The `footer` part has `flexShrink: 0` — which is not `position: sticky`. Also: `root` has no `height: 100%` ("do not claim height: 100% here").

So SFCC-801's **sticky Confirm/Apply footer is a genuinely new behaviour** — no existing component does it. The closest real implementation is `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/zimmCartDrawer.css.ts`, which builds a **second, inner scroll container** (`scrollArea` with `flex:1; minHeight:0; overflowY:auto`) inside the drawer so `body` and `footer` are siblings with independent scroll — but even there the footer deliberately scrolls into view rather than sticking. **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmAuthDrawerContent/index.tsx`** — the "content organism composed into a drawer by a separate container" pattern, with a `description?: string` prop (exactly the optional description SFCC-801 wants) rendered via a `styles.description` recipe part, plus `initialFocusRef` threading. **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmPdpDrawer/index.tsx`** — thin composition: `<ZimmDrawer isOpen onClose size aria-label>` wrapping `ZimmTabs` + content. ### 12. FLAG ICONS

**Flags DO exist — 7 of them — and they are already re-exported from the Zimmermann barrel.**

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/icons/index.tsx` lines 53-59 re-exports from the base package:
`FlagCAIcon, FlagCNIcon, FlagFRIcon, FlagGBIcon, FlagITIcon, FlagJPIcon, FlagUSIcon`

| Needed | Flag available |
|---|---|
| AU | **MISSING** |
| US | `FlagUSIcon` |
| GB (uk) | `FlagGBIcon` |
| DE (en-eu) | **MISSING** |

### 13. `ZimmIcon` — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon/index.tsx`

```ts
type ZimmIconProps = { type: ZimmIconType; size?: ZimmIconSize; color?: string }
  & ({ 'aria-hidden': true; 'aria-label'?: never } | { 'aria-hidden'?: never; 'aria-label': string });
```

## A5. What the two guard suites enforce

### `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` (129 lines)

Exists — at the path you gave. **Scope:** walks `overrides/app/components/**` for every `*.css.ts` that declares a `parts: [...]` array (single-part recipes are skipped), then reads the **sibling `index.tsx`** in the same directory.

Enforces:
1. **Every part the component reads off `styles` must be declared in `parts`.** Regex `READ_RE = /\bstyles(?:\.([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*)|\[\s*'([^']+)'\s*\])/g` matches `styles.foo` and `styles['foo']`. Rationale in the header: `parts` gates `variants`/`sizes` but **not** `baseStyle`, so an undeclared part renders fine today and silently stops responding the day a variant is added.
2. **A sibling `index.tsx` must exist** next to every multipart recipe (`componentFound` must be `true`).
3. **Vacuity guard** — the walk must collect something, every collected recipe must have `declared.length > 0`, and at least one must have `read.length > 0`.

Practical consequence for a new recipe: if it's multipart, it **must** live at `<dir>/<name>.css.ts` beside an `index.tsx`, and `parts` must be a superset of every `styles.X` read in that `index.tsx`. `//` line comments are stripped before both regexes run, so commented-out `styles.foo` won't false-positive, and inline comments inside the `parts` array are tolerated.

### `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` (375 lines)

Exists. **Scope:** walks the registered map — `components` from `./index` plus the composed `theme` — so **anything you add to `index.ts` is immediately under these five assertions.** It resolves function-form `baseStyle` across **all 2^5 = 32 boolean prop combinations** (`inverse`, `disabled`, `hasError`, `focused`, `filled`), plus `variants` and `sizes`.

Six tests:
1. `collect() actually walks the registered recipes` — vacuity guard; `Object.keys(components).length > 0` and `collect().length > 0`.
2. **No sizing property uses a bare spacing-scale key.** `SIZING_PROPS` (`width`/`height`/`minW`/`maxW`/`boxSize`/…) × spacing keys → banned. `width: 'xl'` reads Chakra's `sizes.xl` (36rem), not `space.xl`.
3. **No typography property uses a bare scale key.** `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing` against (own Zimmermann scale keys ∪ spacing keys). Use `textStyle` or `var(--zimm-font-*)`. `fontWeight` deliberately exempt.
4. **No compound shorthand contains a bare scale key.** `padding`/`margin`/`inset`/`gap`/`p`/`m` with a space in the value; `var(...)` is masked out first. `padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser.
5. **House style: no bare token key on a registered scale.** `SPACE_PROPS` × spacing keys, and `COLOR_PROPS` × flattened `colour.ts` keys (dot-paths like `text.default`, `action.primary.bgDefault`) → must use `var(--zimm-scale-*)` / `var(--zimm-color-*)`.
6. **No recipe silently inherits a base SFCC recipe of the same name.** `extendTheme` deep-merges, so any key name that collides with a base recipe inherits it. Allowlist is hardcoded:
   ```js
   const INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu'];
   ```
   **This is the hard constraint on naming a new recipe key: it must be `Zimm`-prefixed (or otherwise not collide with a base SFCC recipe name), or the test fails.** Adding a 4th intentional merge requires editing this array.

Known blind spots documented in the header (both suites are theme/sibling walks, not JSX-attribute scanners): a live failure of mode 2 at `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` (`fontSize="l"`, emits nothing) is unreachable by either suite.

## A5. What the two guard suites enforce

### `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` (129 lines)

Exists — at the path you gave. **Scope:** walks `overrides/app/components/**` for every `*.css.ts` that declares a `parts: [...]` array (single-part recipes are skipped), then reads the **sibling `index.tsx`** in the same directory.

Enforces:
1. **Every part the component reads off `styles` must be declared in `parts`.** Regex `READ_RE = /\bstyles(?:\.([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*)|\[\s*'([^']+)'\s*\])/g` matches `styles.foo` and `styles['foo']`. Rationale in the header: `parts` gates `variants`/`sizes` but **not** `baseStyle`, so an undeclared part renders fine today and silently stops responding the day a variant is added.
2. **A sibling `index.tsx` must exist** next to every multipart recipe (`componentFound` must be `true`).
3. **Vacuity guard** — the walk must collect something, every collected recipe must have `declared.length > 0`, and at least one must have `read.length > 0`.

Practical consequence for a new recipe: if it's multipart, it **must** live at `<dir>/<name>.css.ts` beside an `index.tsx`, and `parts` must be a superset of every `styles.X` read in that `index.tsx`. `//` line comments are stripped before both regexes run, so commented-out `styles.foo` won't false-positive, and inline comments inside the `parts` array are tolerated.

### `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` (375 lines)

Exists. **Scope:** walks the registered map — `components` from `./index` plus the composed `theme` — so **anything you add to `index.ts` is immediately under these five assertions.** It resolves function-form `baseStyle` across **all 2^5 = 32 boolean prop combinations** (`inverse`, `disabled`, `hasError`, `focused`, `filled`), plus `variants` and `sizes`.

Six tests:
1. `collect() actually walks the registered recipes` — vacuity guard; `Object.keys(components).length > 0` and `collect().length > 0`.
2. **No sizing property uses a bare spacing-scale key.** `SIZING_PROPS` (`width`/`height`/`minW`/`maxW`/`boxSize`/…) × spacing keys → banned. `width: 'xl'` reads Chakra's `sizes.xl` (36rem), not `space.xl`.
3. **No typography property uses a bare scale key.** `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing` against (own Zimmermann scale keys ∪ spacing keys). Use `textStyle` or `var(--zimm-font-*)`. `fontWeight` deliberately exempt.
4. **No compound shorthand contains a bare scale key.** `padding`/`margin`/`inset`/`gap`/`p`/`m` with a space in the value; `var(...)` is masked out first. `padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser.
5. **House style: no bare token key on a registered scale.** `SPACE_PROPS` × spacing keys, and `COLOR_PROPS` × flattened `colour.ts` keys (dot-paths like `text.default`, `action.primary.bgDefault`) → must use `var(--zimm-scale-*)` / `var(--zimm-color-*)`.
6. **No recipe silently inherits a base SFCC recipe of the same name.** `extendTheme` deep-merges, so any key name that collides with a base recipe inherits it. Allowlist is hardcoded:
   ```js
   const INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu'];
   ```
   **This is the hard constraint on naming a new recipe key: it must be `Zimm`-prefixed (or otherwise not collide with a base SFCC recipe name), or the test fails.** Adding a 4th intentional merge requires editing this array.

Known blind spots documented in the header (both suites are theme/sibling walks, not JSX-attribute scanners): a live failure of mode 2 at `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` (`fontSize="l"`, emits nothing) is unreachable by either suite.

# SFCC-748 — Breadcrumb and SEO (Contentful content type)

**Mechanically, this is the smallest story of the five.** `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` discovers content types by **directory scan** (`fs.readdirSync` over `scripts/contentful/content-types/`) — there is no index, manifest, or registration list. Dropping a file in *is* the registration.

**To ship one content type:**
1. Add `scripts/contentful/content-types/categorySeo.js`
2. `npm run sync:contentful -- --version-name "SFCC-748 categorySeo"`
3. `npm run install:contentful -- --target dev --dry-run`, then for real; repeat per env in order `dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master`

Plus by convention: `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts` (add `CategorySeoEntry`), a `useCategorySeo.ts` hook + test, a render component + test + story, mount it in `product-list/index.tsx`, and regenerate `.claude/registry/*.md`.

**The exact precedent to copy is `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/scripts/contentful/content-types/sizeGuide.js` + `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useSizeGuide.ts`** — a `key` Symbol with `unique` + `regexp` validation, fetched via a `fields.key[in]=` filter through `useContentfulEntries`, narrowed by `pickMostSpecificByRegion(entries, siteId)` from `overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts`. Arbitrary field filtering **already works with zero hook changes** — `fields.categoryId=X` would work today.

12 content types exist: `footerConfig`, `headerNavItem`, `headerNavigation`, `iconAndText`, `iconAndTextItem`, `image`, `link`, `navGroup`, `region`, `sizeGuide`, `sizeGuideTable`, `uiCopy`. **None keys off a category ID.** `region.siteId` (`unique: true`, not localized) is the only existing SFCC-identifier field and is the right validation shape to copy — but note `region` here means *storefront*, not geography.

**What SFCC-748 genuinely adds:**
1. A Contentful rich-text renderer (see SFCC-749 above — shared cost).
2. **The first localized RichText field in the content model.** No existing type has one; both existing RichText fields are `localized: false`. Editor translation workflow for rich text is unproven here.
3. A decision on locale strategy that **contradicts the established house pattern**: `sizeGuide.js`'s description says *"Locale is encoded in the entry key — do not use Contentful field-level localisation."* SFCC-748's "locale support" needs an explicit call on which way it goes.

**Contentful locale state:** 10 locales provisioned (`en` default, `en-US`, `en-CA`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`), all falling back to `en`. 11 sites → 10 locales (`en-GB` serves both UK and EU-English). Three disagreeing "defaults" in code: `CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE = 'en-US'`, `DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'en'`, space default `en`. Worth settling before a localized SEO body ships.

**Gate cost people miss:** CODEOWNERS:148 routes `scripts/contentful/content-types/` to **tier-2-approvers AND tier-1-approvers**. A one-file story carries a Tier 1 review.

content.text:
Jira's API is timing out under the load from the three remaining agents, so I'll hold the due-date field check. I have enough to give you the plan now.

## 1. The points that already exist

All five are **Ready for Development**, assigned to you, in Sprint 6, and all already have points and written ACs.

| Story | Title | SP |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC-743 | Product Card Group — PWA | **5** |
| SFCC-874 | Product Card Group with Lookbook — PWA | **8** |
| SFCC-749 | Breadcrumb and SEO — PWA Kit | **5** |
| SFCC-748 | Breadcrumb and SEO — Contentful | **3** |
| SFCC-801 | Country/currency selector — PWA | **5** |
| | **Total** | **26** |

## 2. Where those points are wrong

The total is roughly right. The distribution isn't.

**SFCC-874 is overweight at 8 — but only if you build 743 first.** The carousel it needs already exists and is complete (`zimmProductCardMedia` has scroll-snap, arrows, keyboard paging, hover-swap, error fallback). `cardType: Editorial` is one row in an existing config table that the file's own docblock already pre-authorises. Sequenced after 743 it's closer to a 5. Built standalone it's a genuine 8.

**SFCC-749 is underweight at 5.** It's two stories in one coat. It also carries the only copy-first cost of the five (base breadcrumb, PLP page-header, breadcrumb theme file), and READ MORE/READ LESS does not exist anywhere in the codebase — `zimmAccordion` can't do it because its trigger label is a static string with no access to expanded state. I'd call it 8.

**SFCC-801 is underweight at 5.** There is no radio atom in 28 atoms. There's no region→country mapping (`boutiqueRegion` is a store-locator filter, one per storefront, it doesn't group). There are no country display names anywhere — only two-letter codes. And you have 7 flag icons; you need AU, DE, ES, CH, HK, AE which don't exist. I'd call it 8.

**743 at 5 and 748 at 3 look right**, with one caveat on 748 below.

## 3. Grouping

**Package A — SFCC-743 then SFCC-874, same stream, 743 first.**
This is the strongest pairing of the five. 874 is 743's section header plus 743's responsive grid engine, plus a lookbook slot and two prop passthroughs. Build them apart and you pay for the header and grid twice. Worth knowing: the 4-up desktop geometry from SFCC-743's own Figma master is already sitting in `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid.css.ts` with the node reference in a comment.

**Package B — SFCC-748 then SFCC-749, but only loosely coupled.**
748 is the data contract for *half* of 749. The two genuinely shared build items are a Contentful rich-text renderer (doesn't exist, neither story ships its SEO half without it) and a `useCategorySeo` hook. **749's breadcrumb half is fully independent of 748** and can start immediately — the category ancestor data is already on the PLP and PDP pages, and the URL helpers are already built and tested.

**Standalone — SFCC-801.**
It shares essentially nothing with the other four. Its reuse comes from already-shipped infrastructure (`zimmDrawer` gives you right-anchor, mobile full-width, dark overlay and focus trap for free). Its real dependencies are data and design decisions, not code.

## 4. Dates

Sprint is Tue 22 Sep to Mon 5 Oct — 10 working days. Today is day 3, so **7 real build days left**, because 5 Oct is the first Monday of October (NSW Labour Day) and the last day goes to ceremonies anyway. Team review lag is running 2 to 3 days.

| Story | Start | PR open | Merge target |
|---|---|---|---|
| SFCC-743 | Thu 25 Sep | Mon 28 Sep | Tue 29 Sep |
| SFCC-748 | Fri 25 Sep | Mon 28 Sep | Tue 29 Sep |
| SFCC-749 (breadcrumb half) | Fri 25 Sep | Wed 30 Sep | Thu 1 Oct |
| SFCC-874 | Tue 29 Sep | Thu 1 Oct | Fri 2 Oct |
| SFCC-749 (SEO half) | Wed 30 Sep | folded into above | Fri 2 Oct |
| SFCC-801 | — | **does not fit** | — |

## 5. Three things that block a start, not just slow it

**SFCC-748 contradicts two confirmed PRDs.** `dataMigrationSeo.md` (DMU-035) says SEO attributes live in **SFCC per storefront, not Contentful**, with the field schema still open pending Sparro. `plp.md` (SPR-04, confirmed 08 May) says category title/description/hero come from **Business Manager**. The ticket says Contentful. Per the project's own doc-integrity rule that's a stop-and-ask before building.

**SFCC-749's READ LESS contradicts the PLP PRD.** `plp.md` line 18 says the read-more expand is explicitly *"not collapsible — confirmed per 24.06 design review."* Your AC requires READ LESS with focus return.

**SFCC-801's AC is missing two confirmed requirements.** REG-021 mandates a search field inside the selector; REG-022 mandates a warning that changing location may remove bag items. Neither is in the ticket. Separately, `countries.generated.ts` says HK=USD and ME=EUR while `regional.md` says HKD and AED — a selector that prints a currency per row can't ship on top of that disagreement.

## 6. What you're missing

**SFCC-749's breadcrumb is already being built by someone else, right now.** PR #125 (bryanian09's search overlay, draft, changes requested) adds a brand-new `ZimmBreadcrumbs` molecule with its own theme recipe, test and story. It has a `seoText` slot and a READ MORE link. It is not on develop. It does not meet your ACs — the READ MORE navigates away rather than expanding inline, there's no page-context generation and no Contentful wiring. You need to decide today whether you adopt and extend it or let two breadcrumbs exist. If you say nothing I'll plan on adopting it, which makes SFCC-749 dependent on his draft landing.

**SFCC-801 has no design-sourced data to render.** Region grouping exists only as PRD prose, country display names exist nowhere, and six of the flags you need don't exist as assets. The icons rule forbids substituting a visually different one. That's a designer ask you should raise today, not in week two.

**There's a silent trap in SFCC-749 specifically.** The moment `overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/` exists, the existing base-path imports in `product-view` and `staticProductHeader` keep resolving to the **base** file in the real build, not your override. They have to be switched to relative paths in the same change or the work no-ops in production while looking fine in tests.

**Three investigations are still running** — story overlaps across the board, Figma sign-off status per component, and the full Sprint 6 load. Design sign-off is the one that most often sinks a commitment, and I don't have it yet. I'll fold those in when they land.

**Couldn't check:** Figma directly (the connector isn't authorised in this session), and the Jira changelog for who set these points and when — that endpoint is erroring.

## 1. The component-level tracker

**`04.7 Component Inventory` — page ID `400195591`** (SFCC space, currently **version 13**).

Header link at the top of the page: `https://www.figma.com/design/wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/Zimmermann_Design_System_2026?node-id=40000730-13662&p=f&t=XjoPmoD67ZiBFwb9-0`

**Last-updated date: I could not retrieve it.** The Atlassian MCP bridge returns an empty `updated` field on every `confluence_get_page`/`confluence_search` call, and `confluence_get_page_history` failed repeatedly ("Connection closed"). What I *can* evidence: the page is at v13, and its own cell text carries `confirmed by Dennis 2026-08-10` against the Done rows, with a sprint column reading `Sprint 3 for User Story Writing 2026-08-11 - 2026-08-24`. Four of your five will ship this sprint. One won't, and it's SFCC-801, the country/currency selector. Not because it's big. Because there is no design for it. Nobody has drawn it. Monday 28th is the day that decides it. If design hands you the frames by then, you can build it Tuesday to Friday. If not, it can't land. So don't drop it today, put the ask in today.

## Each story, plainly

**SFCC-743, Product Card Group, 5 points.** Build it. Design says done with a minor update outstanding, so chase that update before you start. It's a row of product cards with a title and a link above them. The product card itself already exists and works.

**SFCC-874, Product Card Group with Lookbook, 8 points.** Build it straight after 743. It's the same thing plus a big image on the left. Here's the thing: the image carousel it needs is already built and finished elsewhere in the codebase, and the "editorial" version is one line in a table that already exists. So if you build 743 first, this is realistically a 5, not an 8. If you build it on its own, 8 is right, because you'd rebuild the header and the grid from scratch.

**SFCC-748, Breadcrumb SEO content type, 3 points.** The code is genuinely small. The problem is you need a decision first, and the three points don't include the review. Adding a Contentful content type needs sign-off from the most senior approver group, so a tiny story carries a heavyweight review.

**SFCC-749, Breadcrumb and SEO, 5 points.** This is two stories wearing one coat, and it's underpriced. I'd call it 8. The breadcrumb part you can start now, the data it needs is already on the page. The SEO text part needs a "read more" expander that doesn't exist anywhere in the codebase, and needs a way to render Contentful rich text that also doesn't exist.

**SFCC-801, country selector, 5 points.** Underpriced at 5, but that's academic. See above.

**743, then 874.** Same person, back to back, no gap. 874 is built on top of 743's parts. Do them apart and you build the header and the grid twice, and end up with two versions that drift.

**748 and 749, running alongside.** Start 749's breadcrumb half now, it doesn't wait on anything. 748 gives you the content shape for 749's SEO half, so it goes slightly first, but they're not tightly chained.

## The thing that actually threatens this sprint

**Bryan Ian De Vera is building SFCC-874's layout, in Sprint 6, right now.** SFCC-933 "Shop the Look", 5 points, same epic as yours, Ready for Development. One of its variants is described as "single large editorial image on the left with stacked product cards on the right". That is SFCC-874's `qty=2` and `qty=3` cases, word for word in substance. Both tickets also carry the same `showTitleAndLink` switch with the same meaning.

What's genuinely different: his has five other layout variants and carousel arrows; yours has the 3-vs-4 width ratio, the 5-card 2x2 grid, and the tablet hidden-card rule. So it's not a straight duplicate, but the overlap is real and it's happening this week.

**Talk to Bryan today.** This is the single highest-value thing on this list.

**Your breadcrumb already has a ticket.** SFCC-578, sitting unassigned in the SEO epic, same deliverable, same example text. Two other tickets (573 and 570) declare that they depend on 578, not on your 749. So if you ship the breadcrumb, two downstream tickets are pointing at a ticket that never got built.

**Your SEO text block has a competing design.** SFCC-95 specifies the same page region differently: below Recently Viewed instead of above the footer, multiple accordion sections instead of one title and intro, click-the-header to expand instead of a READ MORE link. Not a redundant ticket. A contradictory one. One of the two is wrong.

They disagree on six things, including whether card type applies to the whole group or per slot, and whether the `grid` field exists at all. Your 874 is linked to 887, whose model matches your props. Yours doesn't.

**And SFCC-801 has a true duplicate:** SFCC-467, same component name, same epic, four shared requirement labels, unassigned, no points, not linked to yours.

**Your display counts don't match the Contentful side.** SFCC-743 says 3, 4 or 6 cards. SFCC-744, its Contentful sibling, says 2, 3 or 4. Only 3 and 4 work in both. Someone will find this the day they try to author a 6-up.

Please let me know when this changes, and we can add to our workload for this sprint." The story moved into Sprint 6 on the 21st. Nobody told her. Two defects, both against the product card itself:

I inferred it was a dependency from its title plus the fact that 743 and 874 both compose the same card component. I never opened it to check what the defects were. That's the kind of thing I should verify before it becomes a scheduled step in your week.

Having read it: **it does not block SFCC-743.** Those defects live inside the card. 743 wraps cards in a row with a header. You can build the wrapper perfectly well around a card whose hover animation is broken.

**It's adjacent to SFCC-874, but still not blocking.** TC-05 is a fault in the hover-and-advance logic, which lives in the card's media component. That's the same file 874 needs to touch anyway, because 874's carousel visibility switch needs a new prop added there. So if you're opening that file regardless, fixing TC-05 while you're in it costs you very little.

Take it off the critical path. It isn't one of your five and it isn't gating anything.

content.text:
Yes — and the gate objection I was about to make doesn't hold. I checked.

## The gate argument doesn't apply

I was going to say bundling them drags the component work behind a slower review. It doesn't, because **749 already needs the same approvers 748 does.**

Any new component here has to register its theme recipe in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`, and that file needs tier-two and tier-one approvers. 748's content type needs exactly the same pair. So they're already on the same gate. Bundling costs you nothing in review time.

(Worth knowing generally: that's true of all five stories. Every new component pulls a tier-one approver onto the PR for one line of registration.)

## But the seam is in the wrong place

748 and 749 aren't "Contentful story" and "PWA story". They're three things:

1. **The breadcrumb** — sits in 749. Independent of everything. The data it needs is already on the page. Unblocked today.
2. **The content type** — 748. Blocked on the Contentful-versus-Business-Manager decision.
3. **The SEO text block** — also sits in 749. Needs 748's shape, and needs a Contentful rich-text renderer that doesn't exist yet.

Pieces 2 and 3 are one vertical slice. Piece 1 has nothing to do with either.

So the answer is: **combine 748 with the SEO half of 749, and pull the breadcrumb out to run on its own.**

## Why that's the right cut

Building 748 alone gives you a content type with no consumer. You can't tell if the schema is right until something renders it. And building 749's SEO block alone means guessing the content shape, then reworking it when 748 lands.

The codebase already has this exact pattern working: the size guide is a content type file, plus a hook, plus a component, all built as one slice. Copy that shape.

Meanwhile the breadcrumb is being held hostage for no reason. It could have a PR up Tuesday. Tied to 748, it waits on a decision nobody has made yet.

## What it costs you

749 becomes two PRs against one ticket. That's normal and nobody will blink.

And the SEO half stays hostage to the Contentful decision — but it already was. Splitting the breadcrumb out means at least something from that ticket lands regardless of how that decision goes.

## Revised slots

| | Build | PR up | Merged by |
|---|---|---|---|
| SFCC-743 | today – Fri 25 | Mon 28 | Tue 29 |
| SFCC-749a breadcrumb | Fri 25 – Mon 28 | Tue 29 | Wed 30 |
| SFCC-748 + 749b SEO slice | Mon 28 – Wed 30 | Wed 30 | Thu 1 |
| SFCC-874 | Tue 29 – Thu 1 | Thu 1 | Fri 2 |
| SFCC-801 | Wed 30 – Fri 2 | Fri 2 | Mon 5 |

Same one-PR-a-day cadence as before, so combining costs no calendar. What it buys is that you build the hook and the schema once instead of twice.

**The hard edge:** you need the Contentful-or-Business-Manager answer by **Monday 28**. Past that, the combined slice can't start and the SEO half slips out of the sprint. The breadcrumb still ships either way, which is the whole point of cutting it loose.

content.text:
Because I was hedging against the Contentful decision, and I overcomplicated it. Looking again, the split is wrong as a default.

## Why it's wrong

**The breadcrumb and the SEO text are one component, not two.** The Figma node is literally "Breadcrumbs/SEO" as a single thing. And the component bryanian09 is already building in PR #125 has both in one file — a breadcrumb trail with a `seoText` slot beside it.

So splitting means you open the same file on Tuesday, ship it, then reopen it Thursday to add the half you left out. Two review cycles, two CodeRabbit runs, two sets of conflicts against a develop branch that's moving fast, and a ticket that sits half-merged and can't go to Done for a week.

For a 5-point story that's pure overhead.

**And the breadcrumb half isn't as clean as I made out.** Its first AC says a breadcrumb on every page. Category pages have the data, but home, cart, checkout, account and the rest don't, and there's no shared page-context object to derive it from. Closing that gap means adding a provider in `_app`, which carries the heaviest review gate in the repo. So the "unblocked half" has its own complication I glossed over.

## What I should have said

Keep 749 whole. Build it with 748 as one slice.

The split isn't the plan, it's the **fallback**. If the Contentful-or-Business-Manager answer hasn't arrived by Monday 28, then you split, ship the breadcrumb on its own, and let the SEO half slip out of the sprint. That way something lands regardless.

Until Monday, plan for it whole.

## Revised

| | Build | PR up | Merged by |
|---|---|---|---|
| SFCC-743 | today – Fri 25 | Mon 28 | Tue 29 |
| SFCC-748 + SFCC-749 | Fri 25 – Wed 30 | Wed 30 | Thu 1 |
| SFCC-874 | Tue 29 – Thu 1 | Thu 1 | Fri 2 |
| SFCC-801 | Wed 30 – Fri 2 | Fri 2 | Mon 5 |

Four PRs instead of five, spread Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. Less review churn than the version I gave you a minute ago.

**Monday 28 is the decision point.** If the Contentful answer is in, 748 and 749 run as one build and both close. If it isn't, you break the breadcrumb out that morning and 749 partially ships.
